title: Tormach microARC 4 (4th axis): A rotary in the machine file and the PathPilot post

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Split from #131 (Support Tormach machines), whose 3-axis work shipped in PR #162. The contributor has a **microARC 4** on a 770MX and can run hardware tests.

**What's wanted:** 4-axis indexing (and, if it proves safe, wrapped A-axis milling) on a Tormach mill with a 4th axis, posted by the Tormach PathPilot post:
- **Machine file:** an A rotary axis about X: travel, max rate and its direction sense. Optional add-on files for the 770MX/1100MX with the microARC 4, or a 4th-axis option on the existing Tormach `.mch` files.
- **Post (`tormach.cps`):** A words in the PathPilot (LinuxCNC) dialect. Rotary feed under G94 for a combined linear and rotary move, or inverse-time `G93`, whichever PathPilot documents. Indexing as positioning-only, with the A move never combined with a cut.
- **Refusals by name:** an A position past travel; a tilted plane the 4th axis can't reach; continuous wrapping, if PathPilot's rotary handling (wrapped or unwrapped A) isn't confirmed.

**Sources:** the user supplied Tormach's public owner's guides, used for behaviour only per the Clean-Room Protocol:
- **TD10749:** *Owner's Guide: microARC 4 - 100 mm 4th Axis* (1223A). PN 38412 is a harmonic-drive 100 mm 4th axis. It needs **PathPilot v2.7.2 or later**, with the 4th-axis type set under **Settings > 4th Axis Rotary**. It mounts on the left or right of the table, keyed to the T-slots, so **A rotates about X**. Mounted on the left with an ATC, there's 10 cm from the TTS flange to the tool tip.
- **TD10552:** *4th Axis, M/MX series* (0626A), and **TD10374:** *4th Axis, PCNC 1100 / PCNC 770* (0626A). These are the older rotary tables: manual table clamps and brake shoes (no clamp M-code), and backlash set to 60-90 arc-seconds.
- Plus LinuxCNC's public G-code reference for rotary axes (G93/G94, A words) and PathPilot's public documentation.

**Open questions to settle first, in a comment:**
1. Does PathPilot wrap A (a rollover axis) or treat it as linear degrees? This decides how a multi-turn wrap posts.
2. Is there an A-axis clamp or brake M-code on the microARC 4? The older tables clamp by hand, so the post would write none and add an operator note.
3. Feed for combined XYZA moves: G94 degrees-per-minute semantics on LinuxCNC, or G93.

Effort: high, under the safety floor (it changes posted G-code and adds an axis).

**Done means:**
- The Tormach machine files can declare the microARC 4 as an A axis.
- The Tormach PathPilot post writes indexed 4-axis work, refusing by name what it can't state.
- Pinned by post tests and a golden.
- Checked in PathPilot Hub, then on the contributor's 770MX with a microARC 4.

Part of #131.
